AGENTS.md
# Baseline — Static Foundation

Read `baseline.config.json` and `README.md` first. This project uses Astro static
output, file-owned content and the shared Baseline design system. Keep the npm
lockfile and use `npm ci` once it has been created by the initial `npm install`.

Use the checked-in `new-site-workflow`, `site-art-direction`, `astro-site-design`
and `impeccable` skills for the applicable brief, art direction, calibration and
public Astro implementation stages. Their EmDash-only sections do not apply to
this profile. Do not load CMS setup/modeling/plugin skills or add database,
React, server-adapter or EmDash dependencies. `static-sveltia` adds the pinned
admin SPA and paired form only; read `docs/sveltia-cms.md` for OAuth proxy/PAT setup.
Keep site decisions in their established home: here by default, or in an explicitly
adopted optional `PROJECT.md` linked here. Keep working rules and the compact Art
Direction Record in this file. `PROJECT.md` holds brief, scope, ownership and
nonvisual rationale; the selected optional `DESIGN.md` holds visual references
and interchange. CSS and configuration own implemented values. Keep one home per
fact, link actual sources, and resolve disagreements by subject and evidence.
Current progress belongs in the existing tracker or a short handoff when needed.
Missing optional records do not block authorized work. See `docs/project-context.md`
and `PROJECT.example.md`; neither creates an extra checkpoint or approval claim.

During new-site design setup, follow `new-site-workflow`'s **Layout spacing choice**
in either track: briefly explain responsive spacing for sections, content groups,
grids and article text. Express defaults to shared spacing and brief-led density
(balanced when unspecified); ask about custom spacing only for a real unresolved
design decision. Follow the skill's discovery questions and Express defaults,
reuse prior answers and record visual direction, density and exceptions with the
Art Direction Record here. Keep approved/assumed nonvisual decisions and
content/maintenance ownership in the established context home. An
authorized autonomous build may use an explicit recommended assumption. Keep
the current shell policy for both choices; custom layouts use tokens and explicit
primitive controls. No settings panel or external-product terminology is needed.

## Shared design authority

`src/styles/global.css`, the layout primitives, `SiteShell.astro`, `design:tokens`
and `check:art-direction` are canonical. Before client-specific visual work,
save a complete `## Art Direction Record` with Aesthetic Lane, Narrative Metaphor,
Typography Pairing (Display and Body), Token Physics (Canvas, Action/Accent,
Borders, Spatial Density), and two or three semicolon-separated Site Anti-Patterns.
Run `npm run check:art-direction -- --require-record` before implementing that work.

This reusable foundation has no invented client art direction. Starter infrastructure
exceptions are exact-path, LF-normalized SHA-256 records; any edit invalidates its
exception. Never add broad directory exceptions or exempt client implementations.
The changed-source check also validates all visual files before Git initialization.
Run `npm run design:tokens -- --init-client --lane <lane>` when adapting the starter,
then calibrate real components at the Component calibration path printed by
`npm run dev` (`/_styleguide/` with the default slash policy) and record results in
`audit/component-calibration.md`. A generated calibration checklist is not evidence
that browser verification has been performed.

## Content, assets and rendering

Posts live in `src/content/posts/`, with a typed schema in `src/content.config.ts`.
`draft: true` excludes a post from listings and generated routes. Detail routes use
`getStaticPaths()` and `render()`; render native Markdown through `<RichText><Content /></RichText>`.
All authored CSS must stay in `@layer base` or `@layer components`; use
`<Section>`/`.section` for page vertical rhythm and `RichText` for editorial flow.
Site settings and navigation live in `src/config/site.ts`.

Base explicitly selects `SiteShell spacingPolicy="automatic-v2"`; shared SiteShell defaults to legacy for reviewed upgrades. Section owns block padding and a container gap, Container owns a content stack gap, Grid owns its grid gap, and the shell owns horizontal gutters once. `spacing="none"` removes padding only; nested modes reset. Use `layout="custom"` for caller-owned display/gaps; breakout retains its named grid. Avoid flow/space-y margins on gapped groups. RichText supplies `.flow` and `data-editorial-content`; generic flow only spaces direct siblings. Mark composite internals `data-editorial-island` and establish editorial bodies deliberately. `flow={false}` removes both behaviors, wrapperless unless attributes require a plain wrapper.

For day-2 spacing requests choose the smallest scope: existing `@theme` scale for global density, regular root `--layout-*` alias for a structural relationship, layered regional alias, primitive `gap`, then an explicit utility exception. Preview `npm run design:tokens -- --set "--root:--layout-grid-gap=calc(var(--spacing-grid) * 0.75)" --json`; review, then add `--write` (and `--write-calibration` for saved-source evidence). Keep CSS authoritative without panels or a second configuration store. See `docs/design-framework.md` and `docs/native-composition.md`; inspect affected pages/styleguide at narrow/intermediate/wide widths after verify/build.

Store content imagery in `src/assets/` and use native Astro image processing with
accurate alt text and native bounds. Reserve `public/` for deliberate unchanged
URL assets, including the Sveltia admin SPA when selected. There is no media
storage endpoint or live CMS editing canvas. Sveltia edits the same Markdown files,
requires a rebuild to publish, and must keep its form paired with the native schema.

## Verification and release

Run `npm run verify`, `npm run build` and `npm run check:dev-tools`. Inspect the
public routes, emitted images, keyboard focus and narrow reflow in a browser.
`/_styleguide` exists in development and isolated fixture builds, and is absent
from production. Never deploy `dist-fixtures/`. Deploy only a verified `dist/`.

Generated CI uses clean `npm ci`, token/art checks, tests, typecheck, static build
and production isolation checks. Commit the initial project-specific lockfile.
Stage shared-source/skill updates with `sync:baseline -- --ref <immutable-SHA>`,
review the incoming files, then apply with `--apply <SHA>` and reverify.
Locally modified tokens/components are conflicts for manual review. Routes,
content, settings, site-owned Base layout, admin config and package definitions
are excluded. Read `docs/baseline-updates.md`; keep managed provenance tracked.
Do not invoke EmDash registry/database/screenshot harness commands on this profile.
Record static browser and deployment evidence in project notes. Before Sveltia
editor handoff test real login, upload, save, rebuild and logout on the deployment.

Template verification requires Node `^22.22.3 || ^24.16.0 || >=26.3.0` (Node 24 LTS recommended). Run `npm run lint:templates` for Astro accessibility checks; `npm run verify` also retains script syntax, tokens, tests and type checking.

## Art Direction Record

- **Aesthetic Lane:** Editorial Paper — warm archival print craft with high serif/sans typographic contrast
- **Narrative Metaphor:** Archival cotton bond paper, deep espresso letterpress ink, and engraved column rules
- **Typography Pairing:** Display: Georgia, Body: System Sans (high-contrast editorial serif headlines paired with clean humanist sans body)
- **Token Physics:**
  - Canvas: Warm archival paper ground (oklch(97.5% 0.012 82)) with cream card surfaces (oklch(99.2% 0.006 85))
  - Action/Accent: Editorial terracotta action (oklch(42% 0.15 28)) with warm ivory label ink
  - Borders: Crisp 1px editorial rules (oklch(86% 0.018 78)) and tailored 0.25rem card corners without drop shadows
  - Spatial Density: Generous editorial pacing (clamp(3.25rem, calc(1.25rem + 10vi), 9.25rem)) and 64ch reading measure
- **Site Anti-Patterns:** No floating SaaS card shadows; no neon or purple gradients; no uncaptioned decorative stock widgets

README.md
# Baseline static project

This project was assembled from an explicit Baseline allowlist. It uses native
Astro Content Collections, shared design tokens and primitives, and static output.
No database, React integration or server adapter is required. Read
`baseline.config.json` for the selected profile. `static-sveltia` adds a pinned
browser editor at `/admin/`; configure the new site's repository and authentication
with `docs/sveltia-cms.md` before using it. Pure `static` includes no admin assets.

```sh
npm install
npm run dev
npm run verify
npm run build
npm run check:dev-tools
npm run preview
```

Optional discovery: `npm run baseline:inspect -- --json` reports the installed
profile, commands, skills, source entry points and declared core component props.
See [project inspection](docs/project-inspection.md) for its read-only scope and limits.

For durable client context, optionally adapt [PROJECT.example.md](PROJECT.example.md).
[Document scope](docs/project-context.md) separates the brief, working rules,
selected design reference, implemented source and current handoff.

The first install creates a project-specific `package-lock.json`; commit it and
use `npm ci` for subsequent clean installs. Dependency versions originate from
Baseline's canonical package definition. No source lockfile is copied from EmDash.

Edit `src/config/site.ts` for navigation and site identity, and
`src/content/posts/welcome.md` for sample content. Add Markdown posts to the same
collection. Required fields are title, description and publication date; hero
images require descriptive alt text. Drafts are excluded from both listings and
detail routes. Content changes require a successful rebuild and deployment.

Use the **Component calibration** path printed by `npm run dev` on Astro's local
origin to calibrate the common components. With the default routing policy this
is `/_styleguide/`, including the trailing slash; `/_styleguide` returns 404.
The printed path also follows a configured base or `trailingSlash: 'never'`.
`npm run fixtures:build` and `npm run fixtures:serve` create an isolated static
specimen build in `dist-fixtures/`; open the same canonical path on its local
origin (normally `http://127.0.0.1:4349`). The release checker rejects that artifact.
Normal production builds omit the styleguide route; configure static hosting to
serve `404.html` with status 404 for missing URLs, without an SPA fallback.

Set `SITE_URL` in the build environment to enable public canonical, social and
structured-data URLs. Without it, URL-dependent metadata is omitted rather than
using the build/preview hostname. `src/config/routing.ts` supplies Astro and the
metadata resolver with one base/slash/output policy; its default is directory
output with trailing slashes. `Base.astro` supplies the sole static metadata
renderer through the shared shell's head slot. Posts use their real publication
date and native hero; missing author/update fields stay absent. No editorial
schema changes or public JavaScript are required. Metadata tests run in `verify`;
`parse5` is a development-only parser dependency.

Host the contents of `dist/` on a static host. Astro's preview server is for local inspection.

`baseline.config.json` records the profile and base source commit.
`.baseline/managed-files.json` records source/output hashes and whether assembly
used an uncommitted source tree. These receipts are provenance, not certification
of future edits. Generated GitHub CI runs clean installs, token/art-direction checks,
tests, typecheck, static build and release checks. The first lockfile must be committed.

Use `npm run sync:baseline -- --ref <immutable-40-character-SHA>` to stage shared
component/token/tool/skill updates. Inspect `.baseline/updates/<SHA>/`, then use
`npm run sync:baseline -- --apply <SHA>` and verify. Local modifications are conflicts
for review; content, routes, settings, admin config and npm dependencies are excluded.
See `docs/baseline-updates.md`. The manual upstream workflow verifies a disposable
proposal and uploads a review artifact; it never pushes to the site repository.

Generator 0.4.0 includes per-platform metadata, native Disclosure/Cluster/Sidebar,
Astro accessibility lint and fluid-token diagnostics. Existing sites need explicit
additions before adopting dependent shared files; sync does not install packages,
add scripts or expand managed membership. See
`docs/architecture-hardening-upgrade.md` and its reviewed example patch. Preserve
the site's original provenance, calibrated tokens, Base/navigation and admin config.

Record browser acceptance and deployment ownership in project notes. The EmDash
database audit, site registry and Windows screenshot baseline commands are not
included in this profile.

Template verification requires Node `^22.22.3 || ^24.16.0 || >=26.3.0` (Node 24 LTS recommended). Run `npm run lint:templates` for Astro accessibility checks; `npm run verify` also retains script syntax, tokens, tests and type checking.

name: astro-site-design
description: Design, improve, or rebuild public pages and reusable components in Astro, including WordPress migrations guided by source evidence. Use for presentation work, not EmDash deployment or content-import operations.
---

# Astro site design and implementation

Use `docs/design-interchange.md` for optional DESIGN.md proposals/exports. Lint and inspect mapped-token drift before exporting; preserve fluid expressions and contextual aliases in linked evidence when lossy. Reconcile proposals with AGENTS.md and shipped CSS rather than automatically replacing either. External tool markup still needs the selected profile's content ownership and native image integration.

Build maintainable, accessible Astro pages and components. When a source site or visual reference exists, inspect its actual rendered appearance before implementation; do not substitute a vague textual approximation for visual review.

## Platform presentation boundary

Read `baseline.config.json` first. `static` and `static-sveltia` use native Content Collections, `getStaticPaths()` and Markdown `render()`; skip `building-emdash-site` and all CMS binding/modeling specialists. Existing EmDash API/editor/cache instructions below apply only to `emdash`. Localized static routes follow the project's file/URL model rather than assuming CMS translation groups.

Use shared `src/layouts/SiteShell.astro` for document metadata, global styles, skip link and landmarks. Platform `Base.astro` wrappers supply file-owned settings/navigation or EmDash contributions. Keep queries, widgets and storage out of shared primitives. `Card.astro` accepts ordinary HTML attribute bags; pass edit annotations only from an EmDash caller.

`ResponsiveImage.astro` accepts native Astro ImageMetadata (from `src/assets`) or a resolved URL with dimensions and uses Astro image processing. Do not add a storage endpoint to static sites. EmDash callers resolve storage with `EmDashImage.astro` before presentation. Static RichText wraps native Markdown in `.flow` plus `data-editorial-content`; Portable Text is a platform extension. `flow={false}` relinquishes both defaults, wrapperless unless attributes require a plain wrapper.

Calibrate tokens, typography, layout, cards, ticker and native images on the same common `/_styleguide` on both foundations. EmDash adds Portable Text/storage specimens separately. Static editor-proxy checks explicitly report inapplicable; this is not an editor verification pass. Production builds must exclude the route and fixture artifacts must remain nondeployable. Generated static sites support manual browser acceptance, not the EmDash-specific screenshot/registry harness. Follow the generated README's actual commands.

## Inspect before implementing

For URL-to-Astro migrations, read [references/component-quarantine.md](references/component-quarantine.md). After content and art-direction gates, calibrate real production primitives on `/_styleguide` before broad page assembly. That reference defines open composition versus semantic composites, surface-aware action patterns, the `src/assets/`/CMS image boundary, safe zero-JS LogoTicker slots and written handoffs. Follow its recorded Stage 4.5 gate; preserve the default-production route guard.

For flat screenshots, visual mockups or external interaction recipes, read [references/visual-mockup-workflow.md](references/visual-mockup-workflow.md). It defines evidence metadata, semantic translation, contextual safeguards and clean-source verification without changing upstream skills.

For a WordPress migration or redesign of an existing site, first read [`references/migration-visual-audit.md`](references/migration-visual-audit.md). It defines the route inventory, source evidence, preserve/improve decisions, and final page-by-page QA required for that work.

1. Use available browser automation to inspect the source site before asking the user for screenshots. Capture each distinct page archetype and unique editorial page at consistent desktop and mobile sizes; capture full-page views so content below the fold is included. Sample repeated records with different layouts or fields. Inspect rendered screenshots and, when available, the DOM and computed styles. If the site requires authentication, blocks automated access, or a relevant page/state cannot be reached with available tools, ask only for the missing access or reference rather than inventing the design.
2. Record a compact visual and content inventory: route/page type, content hierarchy, layout, typography, colors, spacing, imagery/crops, repeated components, interaction states, and responsive changes. Record which recognizable elements to preserve and which specific problems to improve. Verify the meaning of functional assets from nearby copy, links, captions, and destinations; do not infer their purpose from appearance alone.
3. Before coding, establish the design direction. For this user's WordPress migrations, default to improving the design unless faithful reproduction is requested. Treat the source as evidence of content, purpose, and identity, not a quality ceiling or pixel target. Write down the brand cues and functional details to retain, the design weaknesses to solve, and the intended improvements in hierarchy, typography, composition, imagery, navigation, and responsive behavior. Do not silently turn it into a different identity, remove distinctive motifs, or replace meaningful source imagery with generic decoration. Read the design-direction and comparison criteria in `references/migration-visual-audit.md`.

For WordPress sources built with Blocksy, Stackable, or Elementor, inspect the relevant theme/builder configuration as well as the rendered pages: global styles, headers/footers, archive/single templates, reusable sections, dynamic fields, responsive overrides, and interactions. A content export or screenshot alone may miss these. Use them to recover the design rules and behavior, then rebuild in Astro; do not copy generated builder markup or CSS. See the [WordPress content migration skill](../wordpress-to-emdash-content/SKILL.md) for a builder-specific inventory checklist.

Treat per-element IDs and generated builder styles as clues about the source, not as a styling API to port. If repeated items such as Stackable cards have individually assigned IDs, colors, spacing, or typography, compare several instances and determine which differences express real content or intentional variants and which are accidental drift. Model the repeated content as data and render it through one Astro component with shared tokens; add only a small number of named variants for deliberate differences. Use IDs only when identity is needed for anchors, labels, or ARIA relationships, not for visual styling. Do not reproduce each card as a hand-styled one-off.

## Implement clean Astro

For a multilingual site, use the locales and default locale agreed during setup. Astro owns locale-aware public routes; EmDash stores each translation as a separate entry in a linked translation group. Pass `Astro.currentLocale` to EmDash entry, collection, menu, and taxonomy queries. Build locale-aware links and a language switcher from available translations, and include canonical/hreflang metadata where appropriate. Keep each locale's content, menus, and publication state intentional; don't assume fallback supplies collection listings or translates UI copy. Follow EmDash's [internationalization guide](https://docs.emdashcms.com/guides/internationalization/) and verify the default locale stays unprefixed so `/_emdash/admin` continues to work.

- Treat WordPress output as reference content and visual behavior, not markup to copy. Rebuild from semantic HTML, accessible controls, and focused Astro components; do not carry over Gutenberg/Elementor/Stackable wrapper trees, shortcodes, or theme-specific CSS as the new architecture.
- Identify repeated site-wide patterns and make reusable layouts/components for them. Use shared design tokens and component-level classes; avoid one-off inline styles and duplicated page CSS when a shared rule or component is appropriate.
- Inspect the project first and follow its existing styling conventions when they are sound. For a new site or a substantial visual rebuild, use the project's fluid token baseline: Tailwind CSS v4 with CSS-first `@theme` tokens, fluid type and spacing scales (including high-contrast `-to-` bridge steps), semantic spacing names, multi-layer OKLCH elevation shadows, and small semantic Astro layout components. Do not migrate a sound existing system just to standardize it. Do not add Tailwind v3 or the legacy `@astrojs/tailwind` integration to a new project; use Astro's documented Tailwind v4 / `@tailwindcss/vite` setup and verify it against the installed Astro version.
- Use a three-tier architecture: (1) CSS design tokens and base rules, (2) semantic Astro structural primitives, and (3) agent instructions/recipes that constrain composition to the first two tiers. Do not recreate a large combinatorial runtime utility framework.
- Define fluid scales mathematically rather than choosing unrelated `clamp()` values by eye. Choose minimum and maximum values and viewport bounds, calculate the linear interpolation, and encode the result as `clamp(min, calc(intercept + slope * 100vi), max)` tokens. `vi` is the default for viewport-wide fluid type and spacing; use `cqi` for a component that should respond to its containing layout only when an ancestor establishes an inline-size query container. Document bounds and keep the min/max legible at zoom and narrow widths. Prefer a small intentional scale with paired steps (for example, type and space steps) over a large list of near-duplicates.
- Choose responsive behavior by what controls the available space: use intrinsic CSS first, then a container query for a component whose placement changes its width, then a media query for viewport-level behavior. Keep user-preference media queries for motion, contrast, and similar settings. A breakpoint should reflect where content stops working; share a named breakpoint only when multiple parts of the site genuinely need the same threshold. Read `references/responsive-architecture.md` when designing responsive components or changing the site's responsive strategy.
- Centralize palette, font, content widths, type, spacing, breakpoints, radii, borders, shadows, layering, and motion values. Use semantic spacing tokens such as content, grid, and container gaps rather than unexplained one-off layout values. In Tailwind v4, map CSS tokens through the appropriate `@theme` namespaces when they should create utilities; retain regular CSS custom properties for semantic aliases and values that should not create utility APIs. Define color primitives in OKLCH where suitable, then define semantic roles such as surface, text, border, action, and status. Derived shade/alpha steps must still be checked for perceptual consistency, theme behavior, and text/control contrast; don't assume a generated shade is accessible.
- Avoid styling through IDs, long high-specificity selector chains, or escalating `!important` overrides. Let Tailwind utilities, shared component classes, tokens, and deliberate cascade layers express the design. Use `!important` only to contain an override for an external style that cannot be changed, and leave a brief explanation.
- Build semantic Astro primitives such as `Section`, `Container` (`width="reading|content|wide"` for standard sections, `breakout` / `.content-grid` for long-form editorial flows with wide callouts/media), and `Grid` when they encode repeated structure or responsive behavior; use `Card` (`<article class="card">` with `.clickable-parent` / `.focus-parent` on the heading link, `--card-*` custom properties, and concentric `--card-media-radius` math) when its content/link contract is consistent. Keep APIs small and explicit. Don't wrap every element or turn Astro into a client-rendered component system.
- Use the shipped spacing ownership in `docs/design-framework.md`: site-owned Base activates `automatic-v2`; shared SiteShell defaults legacy. Section owns padding and container gap, Container owns content gap, Grid owns grid gap, and the shell owns horizontal gutters once. Local modes reset; `spacing="none"` changes padding only. Choose `layout="custom"` for caller-owned display/gap and retain breakout's named grid. Root `--layout-*` aliases reuse existing scales and can be scoped regionally. Generic `.flow` spaces direct siblings; RichText/explicit `data-editorial-content` owns prose controls, bounded at `data-editorial-island` roots. Avoid duplicating a layout gap with flow/space-y margins. Check actual inline-editor select/type/save/reload when changing CMS renderer boundaries. For day-2 changes preview a narrow `design:tokens --set` request, review its diff, write explicitly and verify the saved source plus affected rendered compositions. Do not create a second token store or spacing settings panel.
- Keep utilities and semantic CSS complementary: Tailwind utilities are useful for clear local composition; component classes and Astro primitives own repeated patterns and complex responsive behavior. For macro layout, prefer structural components and named contextual tokens over default-scale guesses such as `gap-7`, arbitrary values such as `p-[22px]`, or duplicated ad hoc media queries. Do not ban every fixed value: a documented local exception is better than distorting a component API. Use breakpoint variants/media queries for real discrete behavior changes, not to patch around a missing fluid token. With Tailwind v4, component `<style>` blocks are separate style contexts; prefer shared CSS variables or classes from the global stylesheet rather than assuming `@theme` values or `@apply` are automatically available there. If using Tailwind directives in a component style, follow the current `@reference` guidance.
- Include accessible interaction tokens and behavior alongside visual tokens: visible focus styles, hover/active/disabled states, reduced-motion handling, adequate target sizes, and sufficient text and non-text contrast. Honor semantic HTML and keyboard behavior; design tokens do not replace accessible markup or testing.
- Treat WCAG 2.2 AA as the default implementation target unless the project names another standard. Accessibility is a design and content requirement, not a final color-check pass: check landmarks/headings, link and control names, keyboard operation/focus, form labels/errors/status, alternatives for meaningful imagery, contrast, zoom/reflow, motion preferences, and pointer targets. Do not claim conformance based only on automated checks; include manual keyboard and responsive checks.
- Keep HTML semantic and responsive, keyboard-accessible, and readable. Use Astro for mostly static rendering and add client-side JavaScript only for interactions that need it. Preserve progressive enhancement where practical.
- Prefer relationship-aware layout over builder spacing hacks: use `gap` for sibling layout, padding for space inside a section or container, and flow spacing for editorial text. Do not create empty spacer elements or use `min-height` as a substitute for content spacing; use minimum heights only for an intentional composition such as a viewport-filling hero, and make it tolerate longer content. Keep text as HTML rather than baking essential copy into images.
- Do not add intrusive patterns just because a source builder makes them easy: avoid unsolicited popups, autoplaying media, decorative single-item sliders, scroll hijacking, and infinite-scroll-only listings. Prefer visible content, pagination, or user-triggered controls. Preserve or add these patterns only for a clear user need, with keyboard operation, reduced-motion support, and a usable non-JavaScript/content fallback as appropriate.
- Connect EmDash data to presentation through well-defined queries and components. Keep event/plugin data fetching and presentation logic separate; a registry sandboxed plugin's API response is data, not a rendered visitor-facing calendar.

## Styling architecture defaults

- In new builds, keep global tokens, reset/base rules, and rich-text flow rules in a small set of global CSS files. Keep repeated page structures in Astro components and page-specific layout in named component classes; use scoped `<style>` blocks for genuinely local exceptions, not as the only home for a design system.
- Keep a project's design values site-specific. This skill defines the architecture and naming discipline, not one fixed brand palette, font pairing, or set of numeric token values. Derive scales from the visual reference and intended content density, then verify them at narrow and wide viewports.
- Treat spacing and type tokens as the default API, not a ban on every fixed value. Fixed values remain appropriate for borders, icons, control hit areas, compact UI details, and deliberate exceptions. Explain repeated exceptions by giving them a named token or component rule.
- Record these conventions in this skill for cross-site behavior. Put project-specific deviations and naming decisions in that site's `AGENTS.md`. Add a shared package or starter preset only after multiple sites demonstrate that the same implementation is worth maintaining; do not create a framework package just to share a short token file.
- Keep the top-level skill focused on the decision rules and workflow. Put detailed interpolation examples, token naming recipes, Astro component contracts, and EmDash Portable Text examples in small, task-specific `references/` documents and tell the agent when to read them. Optional starter snippets can live beside those references as examples, but never copy them unchanged as a site theme: derive colors, type/space bounds, component variants, and content widths from the site's brief and inspected reference. Avoid loading every recipe into context for unrelated tasks.
- When building a new token system, read `references/fluid-tokens.md`; when creating or reworking repeated layouts, read `references/astro-primitives.md`; when rendering CMS rich text, read `references/emdash-content.md`. Load only the relevant reference for the current task.
- Read `references/accessibility.md` when adding a component pattern, interactive behavior, forms, navigation, media, or a validation checklist.

For a multi-page rollout, read [`references/rollout-verification.md`](references/rollout-verification.md) when planning acceptance. It covers task tracking, capture readiness, live enhancement checks, and honest verification scope.

## Implement and review in visual passes

Do not treat the first implementation as finished. For a new design, compare against the brief and chosen visual direction. For a migration, use the source screenshots to verify content, identity, and behavior, then judge whether the new design solves the documented weaknesses; matching weak source styling is not success. Use `references/migration-visual-audit.md` for that comparison.

1. Build the shared shell and representative page archetypes. Render them in the browser at desktop, mobile, and widths where layouts change. Inspect full pages, including lower sections and interaction states, before applying the design to every route.
2. Record concrete findings by route/component and viewport: missing content, wrong image or meaning, lost brand character, weak or generic composition, hierarchy, spacing, typography, contrast, overflow, and broken behavior. Use screenshots and a design critique tool such as Impeccable when available; a critique supplements the source/brief comparison. Prioritize shared token or component causes before page-specific tweaks. If the draft feels flatter, less distinctive, or harder to use than the source, revisit the design direction before expanding it.
3. Fix the findings as a batch, render again, and check that each material issue is resolved without regressing another page or width. Repeat this check for each newly built archetype. Once all routes are implemented, make a fresh full-page pass across every unique page and representative repeated records; fix and recheck any material findings from that pass.

/** A component gap prop wins its local style variable; utilities still own gap. */
export function layoutStyle(style: HTMLAttributes<'div'>['style'], variable: string, rawGap: unknown) {
  const gap = typeof rawGap === 'string' && rawGap.trim() && !/[;{}]/.test(rawGap) ? rawGap.trim() : undefined;

Layout turns product priority into reading order, grouping, rhythm, and usable space. Diagnose the structural problem before moving boxes.

---

## Visitor mode

- **Persuade + Experience:** composition may be asymmetric, fluid, or intentionally disruptive when the selected world earns it.
- **Operate + Read:** predictable structure, stable density, and navigable linearity are affordances.
- **Native:** follow [ios.md](ios.md) or [android.md](android.md) for navigation, insets, adaptation, and touch targets.

Preserve the established visual world. A layout command changes structure inside it; identity replacement belongs to [new-work.md](new-work.md).

## Two isolated assessments

When a sub-agent tool is available and permitted, run these independently; otherwise run them yourself in this order.

1. **Layout assessment:** inspect representative states and viewports. Answer every question below with rendered or source evidence:
   - **Reading order:** Apply the squint test. With detail blurred, can you still identify the primary element, the secondary element, and the major groups in order?
   - **Grouping:** Are related items close and distinct groups separated, or are containers compensating for weak proximity?
   - **Rhythm:** Do tight and generous intervals create a deliberate cadence, or is one spacing value repeated until everything has equal weight?
   - **Structure:** Does the topology match the content and task? Are repeated cards, columns, or sections genuinely equivalent, or merely a framework default?
   - **Density:** Does the amount of information per region fit use frequency, decision complexity, and visitor mode?
   - **Adaptation:** At narrow, intermediate, wide, zoomed, and localized states, what reorders, collapses, wraps, scrolls, or remains fixed? Does DOM and focus order still agree with the visual order?
   - **Extremes:** Do long content, empty states, overlays, sticky elements, safe areas, and small touch targets expose structural failures?
2. **Mechanical scan:** run:

```bash
.agents/skills/impeccable/scripts/impeccable detect --json --scope layout [target files or dirs]
```

Also inspect arbitrary spacing, overflow, stacking, and container behavior the detector cannot resolve. Keep mechanical evidence out of the first assessment, then synthesize both passes before editing. A clean scan cannot prove hierarchy or rhythm.

## Set the spatial thesis

Before editing, name:

- the primary reading or task path;
- what belongs together and what must separate;
- which element leads and which supports;
- the intended density and spacing rhythm;
- how the structure changes across containers, viewports, input modes, and content extremes.

Choose the simplest structural model that expresses those relationships. Use layout primitives according to the relationships they control, and name reusable spacing and container roles semantically.

## Apply

- Group by meaning. Use proximity before adding containers or decoration.
- Create rhythm through deliberate contrast between tight and generous intervals.
- Use a documented spacing scale rather than one-off values. A 4-unit base usually provides the useful middle steps that an 8-only scale misses.
- Let hierarchy follow product priority, not framework defaults.
- Keep distinct content visually distinct without turning every group into an isolated component.
- Make responsive behavior structural: reorder, collapse, reflow, or reveal based on what remains important.
- Prefer container-aware components when the same component appears in different contexts.
- Use `gap` for sibling rhythm when it expresses the relationship more directly than child margins.
- Keep touch targets usable even when their visible marks are small.
- Use depth only when it clarifies state or hierarchy.
- Make optical corrections only after inspecting the rendered result.

Variation is not a goal by itself. Repetition should support recognition; break it only when content or priority changes.

## Verify

- The squint test still reveals the primary, secondary, and major groups in order.
- The reading and task path remains clear at every supported size.
- Related content groups naturally; unrelated content does not blur together.
- Tight and generous spacing create intentional rhythm instead of monotonous repetition.
- Density matches use frequency and content complexity.
- Long text, empty states, localization, zoom, and dynamic content do not break the structure.
- Keyboard, touch, and assistive-technology order agree with the visual order.
- The final mechanical scan has no unexplained findings.

Answer each item with rendered or source evidence, then rerun the scan. Do not substitute a bare “yes” for verification.

When the structure holds, hand off to `$impeccable polish`.

Every variant declares a coarse `density` parameter and authors spacing against `var(--p-density, 1)`.

```json
{"id":"density","kind":"range","min":0.6,"max":1.4,"step":0.05,"default":1,"label":"Density"}
```

Add one structural parameter only when the topology genuinely branches. Follow [live.md](live.md)'s parameter contract.

# Craft floor

Load this after the direction is settled, and build without announcing the checklist. A pinned brief or the committed visual world overrides anything here; your own habit does not. When the design hook is active it already enforces the mechanical checks below as you edit: act on its findings instead of re-auditing each rule.

## Verify

Each of these is a check on the built result, not an intention. Run them together in each batched look at the render, not as separate screenshot trips; the checks share one render.

- **Contrast:** body and placeholder text ≥4.5:1, large text ≥3:1. On colored surfaces tint secondary text from that hue or the foreground; never gray.
- **Depth:** shadows carry an offset and a soft blur. A zero-offset colored halo is decoration.
- **Spacing:** tight groups, generous separation, more space above a heading than below it. Read the computed values.
- **Type:** body measure 65–75ch, display max 6rem, tracking floor -0.04em, balanced headings, obvious scale and weight steps. Run the real copy at every breakpoint and fix what overflows.
- **Motion:** one authored moment, not scattered effects and not one identical entrance on every section. Exponential ease-out from an already-visible default. Reach past transform and opacity: blur, backdrop-filter, clip-path, mask, and shadow belong to the palette when they stay smooth.
- **States:** hover, disabled, loading, error, empty. Plus real content, working controls, responsive composition, keyboard focus.
- **Browser surfaces:** the parts you did not draw still carry the design. Text selection, the caret, custom scrollbars, focus rings, underline offset, and the numerals in tabular data all ship with browser defaults that belong to no design system. Theme them from the palette. This is the cheapest signal that a page was built rather than assembled, and the one models skip most reliably.
- **Copy:** the product's own language. Controls name their action; errors name the problem and the recovery.
- **Coverage:** every brief requirement present and findable within seconds.

## Refuse

These are the category's defaults, not bans: the brief's own words can earn any of them. Reaching for one when the axis is free means you were not deciding; recognizing that means rewriting the element, not softening it.

Page scaffolds:

- Same-size cards of icon plus heading plus text as the page structure. Cards are the lazy container; nested cards are always wrong.
- The hero-metric template: big number, small label, supporting stats, accent.
- A kicker or eyebrow above a heading. This one is a ban, not a default: no brief earns it back. The heading carries its own weight; delete the label and let the heading speak.
- Section numbers (01 / 02 / 03) unless the sequence itself carries information the reader needs.
- A modal for a task that needs neither interruption nor protected focus.

Surface habits:

- Gradient text. Emphasis comes from weight or size.
- Glass and blur as decoration rather than as a specific effect.
- A colored `border-left` or `border-right` above 1px on cards, list items, callouts, or alerts.
- Hard offset shadows (`box-shadow: 4px 4px 0`) outside a world that is actually neobrutalist. The zero-blur block shadow is a costume, not a depth system; a world that did not choose it never earns it as a default.
- Sparklines, progress rings, and soft-shadowed rounded rectangles standing in for content.
- Monospace as a costume for "technical" rather than for code, data, or measurement.
- A system display face (Impact, Arial Black, the platform sans) as the display voice of an own-world page. Source and self-host a face whose character matches the approved lettering; the closest installed font is a failure, not a fallback.
- Unicode glyphs or emoji standing in for an icon system. Icons are drawn, from a real library or authored SVG, in one consistent stroke and weight.
- Geometric masks standing in for organic contours. A circle, polygon, or radial-gradient cutout approximating a photographic subject's edge is the cheap version of the effect and reads worse than omitting it. Derive an alpha matte from the actual image, or produce a cut-out asset.
- Light or dark picked by category. Pick it from the use scene: who, where, under what ambient light.

- Tracking stops at -0.04em. -0.02 to -0.03em usually reads better.
- Declare elevation once, border or shadow. A 1px border under a wide soft shadow is the ghost card. Card radii stay at 12–16px; pills are for small controls.
- Real illustration or none. Sketch-style SVG scenes, `loose-sketch` / `doodle` class names, and `feTurbulence` grain read as amateur. This bans SVG imitating pictures, never SVG doing geometry: crisp vector shapes, diagrams, animated linework, and shader-driven effects remain first-class media. A shaded, perspectived, or figure-bearing illustration is a picture even in line-art style; geometry means shapes a session can specify exactly.
- Backgrounds are surfaces, textured only from the subject's world. `repeating-linear-gradient` stripes and two-axis grid overlays need an actual canvas, map, blueprint, or measuring tool under them.
- Claims and configuration come from supplied truth; label illustrative values honestly. Naming a concept and then ironizing it is not a claim.

The floor holds the mechanics; it never picks the direction. With every check green, spend the page on the committed world, and when torn between refined and committed, commit.
